outcomeNote: Mishna recording two parallel R' Meir/Rabbis disputes.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר לוֹ: ״נֶאֱמָן עָלַי אַבָּא״, ״נֶאֱמָן עָלַי אָבִיךָ״, ״נֶאֱמָנִים עָלַי שְׁלֹשָׁה רוֹעֵי בָּקָר״. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If one litigant «says to» the other: «My father is trusted» to adjudicate «for me,» or: «Your father is trusted» to adjudicate «for me,» or: «Three cattle herders,» who are not proficient in halakha, «are trusted» to adjudicate «for me,» all of whom are disqualified from serving as judges, «Rabbi Meir says:» The one who made the offer «can retract it, and the Rabbis say: He cannot retract it,» but must accept their verdict.

segments.he: הָיָה חַיָּיב לַחֲבֵירוֹ שְׁבוּעָה, וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״דּוֹר לִי בְּחַיֵּי רֹאשֶׁךָ״. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
segments.en: Similarly, one who «was obligated» by Torah law to take «an oath to another,» which is done while grasping a sacred object, «and» the latter «said to him:» Instead of taking an oath, merely «vow to me by the life of your head» that what you claim is true, «Rabbi Meir says:» The one who made the offer «can retract it,» and demand that the other litigant take an oath, as he is obligated to do by Torah law. «And the Rabbis say: He cannot retract» his offer. Once he has agreed to accept a vow, which is of less severity than an oath, he cannot retract his agreement.

moves.summary: Accepting father or cattle herders as judges: R' Meir can retract; Rabbis cannot
Vow by the life of your head instead of oath: same dispute

edges.about: whether one who accepted a disqualified relative or layman as judge can retract
whether one who let his opponent vow by his life instead of an oath can retract

positions.claim: the one who made the offer can retract
